A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same positional-bias study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, passage-position, answer-accuracy, and closed-book experiments on PopQA, NQ, and TriviaQA.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds ColBERT retrieval results and a Claude–Llama judge-agreement study in Appendices A.2.1 and A.3.1.

M1.justification: The distracting-effect calculation and five passage-ordering strategies are unchanged. The additional retriever and judge extend comparisons and validation without revising the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use PopQA, KILT NQ, and TriviaQA with the same Wikipedia corpus and English factoid-QA scope. The added checks reuse this coverage without introducing a new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix A.2.1 adds ColBERT alongside the existing BM25/BGE retrieval comparisons. Appendix A.3.1 newly compares Llama 3.3 70B Instruct with Claude 3.7 Sonnet as evaluators. The five passage-ordering strategies are retained.

E3.justification: A.3.1 introduces a judge-comparison protocol using 100 queries per dataset, 1,500 top-5 BGE passages, 300 generated answers, and Cohen's kappa. The original disjoint 500-query samples and k=5/10 RAG evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: A.3.1 adds an evaluator-validation analysis measuring agreement between Claude and an open-source judge. The original positional analyses and closed-book comparisons remain; the Olympics case is retained with additional distraction-score annotations.

E5.justification: V2 adds statistical agreement estimation using Cohen's kappa in A.3.1. The existing Wilcoxon test and 0.05 threshold are retained, with no added repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: A.2.1 adds ColBERT accuracies of 67.13, 67.20, 67.00, 66.87, and 67.07 for Sequential, Inverse, Shuffle, MaxRelevance, and MinDistraction, respectively. A.3.1 reports relevance/answer judge agreement of 0.85/0.94, and Figure 3 adds per-passage DE values. Matched original tables and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the treatment of relevant passages, and hard/weak distractor thresholds are unchanged. The added agreement metric is used empirically without introducing mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that strong retrievers surface hard distractors, positional bias has limited impact in realistic RAG, and strategic reordering generally performs comparably to shuffling.

C2.justification: A.3.1 newly interprets high judge agreement as supporting Llama 3.3 70B Instruct as an open-source evaluation alternative. Existing explanations involving distractors and parametric memory, and the factoid-QA and English-language limitations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The corpus snapshot, chunking, indexing services, and generation/judging prompt templates are retained. The added studies specify evaluation designs but supply no new implementation hyperparameters, hardware details, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of Chain-of-Note, RECOMP, and FastFiD for filtering or compression. New references also support ColBERT and agreement interpretation. Publication updates to existing references do not represent additional works; the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The title adds 'Really'; short explanations, two appendix subsections, and acknowledgments are added, and an author email is removed. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 13 becomes v2 Figure 3 in the main text, with shortened excerpts, DE annotations, and a revised caption. Appendix figures and tables are relocated or reordered, including closed-book Table 7 becoming Table 5. Existing plot designs and the two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: The ColBERT comparison broadens empirical support, while judge-agreement validation provides a useful reliability check absent from v1. The annotated main-text example and related-work additions improve clarity and context. These are limited gains: inter-model agreement does not establish human-validated correctness, and the principal experiments and claims remain unchanged.
